html:
The Luritja are an Aboriginal Australian people of the Northern Territory, west and southwest of Alice Springs. The map shows them from 1600 to 1815. Their name is said to come from an Arrernte word for strangers, used for the desert peoples to the west.

They were desert dwellers, and their speech is a variety of the Western Desert language of the Western Desert cultural bloc. Their neighbours were the Arrernte to the east, the Pintupi to the northwest and the Pitjantjatjara to the south.

In the 20th century many Luritja lived at the Lutheran mission at Hermannsburg and at the government settlement of Papunya. Luritja men were among the first painters of the Papunya Tula art movement from 1971.
